complete_mirror_norm_proof: Put pi=sqrt(2), epsilon=1+pi, delta=3+pi, and a=2*pi-1, so epsilon*a=delta and (delta) is a prime of norm seven. For primitive r=(x,y), reflection integrality says (q(r)) divides 2I(r), where I(r)=(a*x,(y,D24+)). Even unimodularity excludes every prime away from (pi) and (delta). At (delta), either y is primitive and the valuation is zero, or reflection integrality gives y in delta*D24+; then x is a unit and q=-a*x^2 mod delta^2 has valuation one. At (pi), if x is a unit then q=-a*x^2 mod pi^2 has valuation zero. Otherwise primitivity makes the spatial pairing ideal a unit; evenness gives valuation at least two and q|2I gives valuation exactly two, namely the ideal (2). Since Z[sqrt(2)] has class number one and every totally-positive unit is a square, the complete canonical norms are 1, 2, delta, and 2*delta.

enumeration.prime_seven_divisibility: For q divisible by delta, reflection integrality forces y in delta*D24+; enumerate y/delta at target y^2/delta^2.
enumeration.primitivity: Test divisibility by sqrt(2) in the integral D24+ glue basis; discard norm-2 vectors whose quotient is a norm-1 mirror.
